set.body:
Plan: docs/plans/2026-09-18-best-recall-to-video-mapper.md §3 Phase 3 H3.

'Automatic' today means matching to coder prose. FilmFestival now has local video, frames and ASR for eight films; Sherlock has local video.

Scope:
Development arms per track.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Sub-arm T3: dialogue (the Friends transcript; FilmFestival ASR for the speech films).
2. Sub-arm T4: captions from frames (Sherlock and FilmFestival's eight films) with pinned captioner receipts.
3. Sub-arm T2: crowd descriptions (FilmFestival).
4. An independence ablation (perception-only vs annotation-only) per corpus; results and claims are reported per track.
5. Every model component used has a recorded licence disposition (bd-01M184XP908JX51S3ZYFX20HC7 or docs/design/vlm-captioning-admission-record.md).
6. Each sub-arm has a ledger entry before its first gold read and runs through recall-map on development data only.
7. Each sub-arm is compared with the current best development configuration on the pre-declared participant-average estimand.
8. The outcome of each sub-arm is recorded as adopt, reject or unavailable, with the evidence; adoption changes the shipping candidate only through a committed config change.

Gate (AGENTS.md SD2/SD6): `sbt -batch clean compileAll testAll` on the merge result, then
`sbt -batch scalafmtCheckAll scalafmtSbtCheck` as a separate run; every test task in build.sbt's
testAll alias reports bound totals (56 at 0e36a7fa, after the corpus modules were added; recount if
modules change); a named mutation witness per new guard, and each compile-time-probe mutation proved
after its own clean recompile; `cd docs-site && npm run verify:examples` when public API or examples
change; fresh-context cold review in a separate pass; the commit body states the evidence and what
it does not establish.

Size: L.
set.title: Phase 3 H3: coder-independent inputs (dialogue, captions, crowd) and the independence ablation
